entries.definition: the usual weather conditions of a region over time
entries.example: The region’s dry climate influences the crops people grow.

entries.definition: a statement about expected future conditions
entries.example: The weather forecast suggests rain later this afternoon.

entries.definition: the amount of rain falling in an area
entries.example: Farmers record rainfall to understand changes in their fields.

entries.definition: very bad weather with strong wind and often rain
entries.example: The storm damaged several trees beside the road.

entries.definition: water covering land that is normally dry
entries.example: The village prepared sandbags before the expected flood.

entries.definition: a long period with much less rain than needed
entries.example: The drought forced the farm to change its planting plans.

entries.definition: land beside the sea
entries.example: Small fishing boats returned to the coast before dark.

entries.definition: a very large body of salt water
entries.example: The exhibition follows a research ship across the ocean.

entries.definition: a large natural flow of water across land
entries.example: A footbridge connects the villages on either side of the river.

entries.definition: a small natural flow of water
entries.example: A narrow stream runs behind the school garden.

entries.definition: a large area covered mainly by trees
entries.example: The guide asked visitors to stay on the forest path.

entries.definition: a region receiving very little rain
entries.example: Plants in the desert face long dry periods.

entries.definition: low land between hills or mountains
entries.example: The valley receives sunlight later than the hill above it.

entries.definition: an area of land rising above the surrounding ground
entries.example: We climbed the hill to see the whole town.

entries.definition: the upper layer of earth where plants grow
entries.example: The gardener tested the soil before choosing the plants.

entries.definition: the part of a plant from which a new plant can grow
entries.example: Place each seed in a separate small pot.

entries.definition: the part of a plant that usually takes water from soil
entries.example: A strong root helps the plant stay in place.

entries.definition: a flat plant part that usually captures light
entries.example: The student drew the shape of a leaf.

entries.definition: a part of a tree growing from the main trunk
entries.example: A bird landed on the lowest branch of the tree.

entries.definition: the gathering of crops when they are ready
entries.example: The family invited neighbors to help with the harvest.

entries.definition: a plant grown in quantity for food or other use
entries.example: The farmer chose a crop that needs less water.

entries.definition: animals and plants living without human control
entries.example: Quiet paths make it easier to observe wildlife.

entries.definition: the natural home of a plant or animal
entries.example: The wetland provides a habitat for many birds.

entries.definition: harmful substances or energy entering the environment
entries.example: The class measured noise pollution near the busy road.

entries.definition: unwanted material left after something is used
entries.example: The café sorts its food waste separately.

entries.definition: small pieces of rubbish left in public places
entries.example: Volunteers collected litter beside the river path.

entries.definition: to process used material so it can be used again
entries.example: Our building can recycle paper and certain containers.

entries.definition: to use something again rather than throw it away
entries.example: We reuse clean jars to store rice and beans.

entries.definition: to use a resource carefully to avoid wasting it
entries.example: Fixing the dripping tap will help conserve water.

entries.definition: something useful that people can use or draw on
entries.example: Clean water is a resource that communities must manage carefully.

entries.definition: material used to produce heat or power
entries.example: The new stove uses less fuel than the old one.

entries.definition: a form of energy used to power devices
entries.example: The clinic needs a reliable supply of electricity.

entries.definition: naturally replaced and available again over time
entries.example: The class compared renewable sources with fuels from underground.

entries.definition: relating to energy or light from the Sun
entries.example: A solar lamp lights the path outside the house.

entries.definition: air moving naturally across an area
entries.example: The strong wind made cycling across the bridge difficult.

entries.definition: an area protected from direct sunlight
entries.example: We placed the water bottles in the shade.

entries.definition: a place offering protection from weather or danger
entries.example: The hikers found shelter beneath a sturdy roof.

entries.definition: harm that makes something less useful or valuable
entries.example: The inspection found damage to the outer wall.

entries.definition: the possibility of harm or an unwanted result
entries.example: The team discussed the risk before crossing the river.

entries.definition: something that could cause harm or danger
entries.example: A nearby road can be a threat to small animals.

entries.definition: free from dirt or harmful substances
entries.example: The village protects its supply of clean water.

entries.definition: covered in dirt or containing unwanted substances
entries.example: We washed the dirty tools before putting them away.

entries.definition: connected with a nearby place or community
entries.example: The market sells vegetables from local farms.

entries.definition: one of the main periods into which a year is divided
entries.example: This walking path is different in every season.

entries.definition: containing a lot of water vapor in the air
entries.example: The room felt humid after the heavy rain.

entries.definition: recently produced or not stale
entries.example: The stall sells fresh herbs each morning.

entries.definition: existing in nature rather than made by people
entries.example: The path follows the natural shape of the river.

entries.definition: found often or in many places
entries.example: This common garden bird has a surprisingly varied song.

entries.definition: not found or seen very often
entries.example: Visitors must not pick the rare flowers.

entries.definition: to remain alive despite difficulty or danger
entries.example: Some plants survive dry weather by using stored water.
